channel.title: Unicon Construction — Insights
channel.description: Field reports and engineering commentary from Unicon Construction — bulk water, heavy civils and turnkey infrastructure in Southern Africa.

item.title: Built By Many Hands: How A Trade Gets Passed On, On Site
item.description: Heritage Day is a fair moment to be plain about how skill actually moves on a construction site — through the artisans, foremen and operators who carry it.

item.title: El Niño 2026: What A Dry Summer Does To Water Infrastructure
item.description: A very strong El Niño is forecast for the 2026/27 summer. Drought does not break water infrastructure, it exposes the parts that were already marginal.

item.title: Small Bridges, Serious Engineering: Building River Crossings in Rural KwaZulu-Natal
item.description: Box culverts, low-level crossings and river bridges rarely make headlines — until the road washes out. Notes from nine KwaZulu-Natal river crossings.

item.title: What a Water Treatment Works Upgrade Actually Involves
item.description: Abstraction, flocculation, clarification, filtration and storage, and what changes when the plant must keep supplying a town while you rebuild it.

item.title: The Critical Role of 40ML Reservoirs in African Water Security
item.description: An in-depth look at the engineering requirements and post-tensioning techniques necessary to construct zero-leakage bulk water storage in hostile topographies.

item.title: Bridging Civil Mastery with Biological Harmony
item.description: Unicon Construction's alliance with JWE Africa brings 30 years of animal rearing and agro-processing design into turnkey agricultural EPC delivery.

item.title: Launching 2027: Predictive Facility Management
item.description: Unicon previews its upcoming 2027 Facility Management division, utilizing IoT sensors and drone structural health audits to protect R100M+ assets.
